clue.text: Ultimately, saddest tear to go viral

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of saddest
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: A heartbreaking tearful moment spreads across the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as the drop from a crying eye, but it is the verb meaning rip.
explanation.definitionFit: To trend is to become suddenly popular online, which is exactly what spreading virally means.

clue.text: Locates characters up to four times in an election-night report

indicators.note: the letters of the word may each be reused, up to four times apiece, and arranged in any order

parts.note: first use: all seven characters
second use of four of its characters
third use of two of its characters
fourth use of one character, the limit the clue allows

explanation.surface: A tally of where characters appear, repeated four times over, on election night.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: TOO CLOSE TO CALL uses only the letters of LOCATES, with O appearing four times, L three times and the others fewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters say a race is too close to call when the vote counts are tied so tightly no winner can be projected.

clue.text: Home for some Europeans drifting into sea

indicators.note: drifting things wander out of place, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Migrants' homes are floating out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, the homeland of the Estonians, who are Europeans.

clue.text: Intended to rise up and corral man losing head to Alzheimer's, perhaps

indicators.note: to corral is to pen in, so one piece is enclosed by the other
in a down entry, rising up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: aimed means intended

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's first letter is removed

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A plan to stage an uprising and round up a man whose mind is failing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'rise up' means the word is read from the bottom upward; 'losing head' drops only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of dementia, so it is an example of the condition.

clue.text: Those who aren't expert mostly gather to admit true failing

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is placed inside the other
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to amass is to gather together

indicators.note: something failing has broken down, so its letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Novices tend to gather and confess that something genuine has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: AMASS loses its last letter to become AMAS, which then takes in the scrambled TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs are non-professionals, people lacking the skill or training of an expert.

clue.text: Pilot's instrument to measure duration and make changes outside

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to alter is to make changes
to time something is to measure how long it lasts

explanation.surface: A cockpit gauge that clocks durations and can be adjusted from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter tells a pilot the aircraft's height above sea level, a key flight instrument.

clue.text: 15 circling around near deep hole

indicators.note: circling around means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the answer to 15 across means fool, and so does ass
by means near, as in standing by

explanation.surface: A fool walks in circles near the edge of a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 15 does not give its own letters here: 15 across is TWIT, and the wordplay wants a synonym of it, ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a chasm so deep it seems bottomless.

clue.text: Extra performance before capturing military figure

indicators.note: capturing means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A bonus show put on before the arrest of a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an additional piece performed after the main show at the audience's request.

clue.text: Outspoken rule: "Male lover is a gay symbol"

indicators.note: outspoken points to words as they are spoken out loud rather than written

parts.note: to reign is to rule
a beau is a male sweetheart

explanation.surface: A frank slogan declaring that a man's boyfriend is a gay emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow flag is the widely recognised emblem of LGBT pride.

clue.text: Notable's constituents repeatedly used a traveler's official paper

indicators.note: the component letters may be used more than once each, in any order

parts.note: first use: every character, with the S from the possessive
second use of five of its characters
third use of one character

explanation.surface: A dignitary's voters keep using a passport-like document.
explanation.walkthrough: As at 1 down, the answer uses only the letters N, O, T, A, B, L, E and S, several more than once. Constituents doubles as voters in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone away from home on election day votes by absentee ballot, an official voting paper.

clue.text: "Looking at the eyes of a cat" in slightly rewritten poetry

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a text rewritten slightly has its letters only lightly reordered

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A line about gazing into a cat's eyes, quoted from a verse that has been lightly edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly' is fair: only the first two letters of the poem word change places. A tom is the usual crossword cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Optometry is the profession of examining eyesight, testing vision and prescribing lenses.

clue.text: Branch following Celsius scale

indicators.note: following places the first word's letters after the second's

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Celsius
a limb is a branch of a tree

explanation.surface: A tree branch is graded on the Celsius temperature scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks like a noun for measuring temperature, but it is the verb meaning go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or mountain is to climb it, ascending its height.

clue.text: Fifty-nine shredded sheets

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: shredded means torn to pieces, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fifty-nine pages have been put through the shredder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty-nine' looks like one number, but it splits into L and a jumbled NINE; the sheets are bedding, not paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a collective name for household bedding such as sheets and pillowcases.

clue.text: Pitiful distance holding back shows

indicators.note: holding means one piece keeps the other inside it

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word from its end to its start

parts.note: to bare something is to show it

explanation.surface: A sorry stretch of road keeps the performances away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something wretched and deserving of pity or contempt.

clue.text: Proponent of government control "fudged" (sic) data

parts.note: a statist favours strong central control of the economy

indicators.note: fudged figures have been doctored, so these letters are tampered with and reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big-government advocate is accused of fudging the data, with a scornful (sic) for good measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and (sic) look like an editor's sneer, but sic is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Statistics are numerical facts collected for analysis, a common synonym for data.

clue.text: Barrel maker took in work with others

parts.note: a cooper makes barrels
to eat something is to take it in

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker took on a job working with a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took in' looks like a container instruction, but it is simply ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to act jointly with others towards a shared goal.

clue.text: Ford model accompanied by short fool

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Henry Ford's Model T car
with means accompanied by

explanation.surface: A Ford car shows up with a little idiot in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford model' suggests a fashion model from the Ford agency; it is the Model T car.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly, foolish person, a mild insult meaning a fool.

clue.text: Denigrate flower: "It's a catastrophe"

parts.note: to dis someone is to belittle them
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Someone running down a bloom declares it a total failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamitous event, the same thing as a catastrophe.

clue.text: Incapacitate a demonstrator, perhaps, in just a second

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary of just and a and second

explanation.surface: Police can disable a protester in a matter of seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: To tase someone is to stun them with a Taser, incapacitating them, as police may do to a protester.

clue.text: Leaves church after terrible pains

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second
terrible means in a bad state, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of church after suffering awful aches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb for walking out; it is the noun, green leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy vegetable eaten for its leaves.

clue.text: Premium stocks (or, the thing I consider most important)

indicators.note: a shop that stocks goods holds them inside, so the following pieces go within

parts.note: a premium is a prize or reward
taken as written
it is the pronoun for a thing
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor names the high-value shares that matter to them most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premium stocks' reads as a finance phrase, but premium is the outer word and stocks the instruction. PRIORITIZE is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To prioritize something is to rank it first, treating it as the most important item.

clue.text: Fashionable religions? They might be creepy

parts.note: in means fashionable
sects are religious groups

explanation.surface: Trendy faiths that some people find unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creepy' seems to describe cults; it is a pun on creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs crawl, and creepy-crawlies is a common name for them.

clue.text: Stick your _____ ! (Contact [email protected])

wordplay.note: the blank on the familiar poster notice is filled by two short words: the abbreviation for advertisement and a word meaning in this place

explanation.surface: A billboard notice inviting advertisers, with an email address to contact.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the advertising notice is completed by two words, AD and HERE, which read together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: To start diesel vehicle in South American country is a family responsibility

indicators.note: in places those pieces inside the country's name

parts.note: the country on South America's Pacific coast

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of diesel
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Starting the family's diesel car in Chile is a parent's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after young children is a duty that falls on a family, so childcare is a family responsibility.

clue.text: I understand: Keeping record is the beginning

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: aha is the exclamation of sudden understanding
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that holding on to records is where it all starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter, so it stands for the start, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Leaders of all the service economies are confused

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the five words all, the, service, economies and are

explanation.surface: The heads of every service-based economy are baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like the link to the definition, but it supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for feeling lost and bewildered.

clue.text: Contract rebel to smuggle arsenic

indicators.note: smuggled goods are hidden inside something, so one piece is tucked within the other

parts.note: Robert E. Lee led the rebel Confederate army in the US Civil War
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: An insurgent is hired to sneak poison past the guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' suggests a hit job for the rebel, but it is the noun: a rental agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a legal agreement letting property for a set term, a kind of contract.

clue.text: When returning resinous substance the first time, to complain is useful

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: lac is the resin secreted by an insect, the source of shellac
I is the Roman numeral one, the first
T is the abbreviation for time
to carp is to complain pettily

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a resin on first encountering it turns out to be worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first time' reads as a single phrase; it splits into the first (I) and time (T).
explanation.definitionFit: Something practical serves a real purpose in use, which is what being useful means.

clue.text: Astonishingly, Chelsea swallowed a ring and a string

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower
astonishingly suggests something turned upside down, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Chelsea, amazingly, gulped down a ring and a piece of string.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a district of London and a football club, but here only its letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoelace is the cord or string threaded through a shoe's eyelets to fasten it.

clue.text: Steer badly and start over

indicators.note: done badly, the word is mangled into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver who steers poorly has to begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset is to restore to a starting point, beginning again from scratch.
